title: No scholastic catechism required — God wrote by their hands
source_text: XIV. At, inquit Bellarminus, si doctrinam sacram literis consignare ex professo voluissent, certe catechismum aut similem librum confecissent. At ipsi, vel historiam scripserunt, ut Evangelistae: vel epistolas, ut Paulus & alii, in quibus nonnisi obiter de dogmatibus tractant. Respondeo scriptores sacros non tam scripsisse, quam Deum per ipsorum manus: Deum autem in scribendo humanae & scholasticae methodo astrictum non esse; Imo istas scholae leges scripti divini majestatem & simplicitatem non satis decere. Quomodocunque vero scripti sint libri sacri, inde satis facile & luculenter doctrina fidei, & praecepta vitae ab attentis & piis lectoribus colligi possunt. Certe negari non potest Mosen saltem ex aperto & expresso Dei mandato legem a Deo acceptam literis mandavisse. Neque tamen libros magis methodicos scripsit, quam Apostoli & Evangelistae. Sed in libris Mosaicis sine ullo certo ordine sparsa sunt praecepta Dei, & historiis variis inserta.
pass_a_gloss: But, says Bellarmine, if they had professedly meant to consign sacred doctrine to letters, they would certainly have composed a catechism or similar book. Yet they either wrote history, as the Evangelists, or epistles, as Paul and others, in which they treat of dogmas only in passing. I answer that the sacred writers did not so much write as God wrote through their hands: and God in writing is not bound to human and scholastic method; Indeed those school rules do not sufficiently befit the majesty and simplicity of divine writing. However the sacred books are written, from them the doctrine of faith and the precepts of life can be gathered easily enough and clearly by attentive and pious readers. Certainly it cannot be denied that Moses at least, by God's open and express mandate, committed to letters the law received from God. Yet he did not write more methodical books than the Apostles and Evangelists. But in the Mosaic books God's precepts are scattered without any fixed order, and inserted among various histories.
pass_b_english: Bellarmine wants a catechism; he finds only Gospels and letters that touch dogma in passing.
Reply: God wrote through their hands — not bound to school method.
Pious readers can still gather faith and life-precepts from the books as written.
Moses had an express write-order yet left precepts scattered in narrative — same pattern.
